name: Google Workspace
text_content:
What it is: Google's business productivity and collaboration platform. The infrastructure layer for email, calendar, file storage, and video meetings at FNHG. Superhuman sits on top of Gmail as the email client — Google Workspace provides the underlying mailboxes, storage, and deliverability.

Products in use:

Gmail — email infrastructure and hosting. Superhuman is the client; Gmail owns the mailboxes and data
Google Meet — video conferencing, internal team calls, vendor meetings. Replaces Zoom
Google Calendar — calendar and scheduling infrastructure beneath Superhuman
Google Drive — file storage (evaluate against Box; may consolidate here)
Google Business Profile — separate from Workspace but part of the Google ecosystem; manages local SEO and reviews

Functions in stack:

Email Hosting & Infrastructure
Video Call Hosting (Google Meet)

Relationship to other tools:

Superhuman uses Gmail as its backend — Superhuman is the interface, Google Workspace is the data layer
RingCentral handles phone; Google Meet handles video — no overlap
Box and Google Drive may overlap on file storage — evaluate and consolidate

Pricing: Business Starter ~$6/user/month; Business Standard ~$12/user/month (includes larger Meet limits and more storage). Confirm tier based on team size and storage needs.

name: Josh.ai
text_content:
What it is: AI-powered building automation platform for luxury hospitality and residential environments. Sits as the control orchestration layer on top of existing hardware (Lutron lighting, Ecobee HVAC, Soundtrack audio) and unifies them into a single scene-based system with natural language voice control.

Core capabilities:

Unified scene control: one command triggers lighting (Lutron), temperature (Ecobee), and audio (Soundtrack) simultaneously
Natural language voice control — privacy-first, all processing on-device
Daypart automation: scheduled scene transitions (Good Energy → Dosi → Sŏn → Luxx) execute automatically
Third-party integrations: native Lutron HomeWorks QS integration, Ecobee integration, plus 100+ smart home and commercial platforms
Mobile app and keypad control in addition to voice
Used in high-end hotels, luxury residential, and premium commercial environments

Functions in stack:

Daypart Lighting Transition Automation (orchestrates Lutron)
HVAC Zone Scheduling (orchestrates Ecobee)

Relationship to other tools:

Lutron HomeWorks QS + Ketra: hardware and scene storage layer — Josh.ai calls Lutron scenes, it doesn't replace them
Ecobee: thermostat hardware — Josh.ai sets zone setpoints, Ecobee executes them
Soundtrack: Josh.ai can trigger Soundtrack zone transitions as part of a unified scene command

Why Josh.ai over individual controls: Four daypart transitions per day across lighting, HVAC, and audio. Without a unified layer, each transition requires manual action across three separate systems. Josh.ai reduces all four transitions to scheduled automation — the room transforms itself.

Privacy note: Josh.ai is explicitly privacy-first; unlike Alexa/Google Home, voice processing is on-device, no audio sent to cloud. Appropriate for a fine dining environment where customer conversations should not be captured.

name: Ecobee
text_content:
What it is: Smart commercial thermostat and HVAC control system. Manages building temperature and energy across multiple zones with daypart-aware scheduling.

Core capabilities:

Zone-based temperature scheduling: different setpoints per daypart and occupancy level
Demand-based control: adjusts HVAC based on occupancy patterns
Energy reporting and efficiency analytics
Utility rebate eligible in Austin (Austin Energy Smart Thermostat rebate program)
Remote management dashboard
Third-party integration via API

Functions in stack:

HVAC Zone Scheduling
Building Energy Monitoring

Critical operational context: A Korean live fire kitchen with 4,000–6,000 CFM exhaust hood volume requires precise HVAC management. Kitchen must run slightly negative pressure relative to dining room per ASHRAE Standard 154. Four dayparts across a 16-hour operating window create significantly different occupancy loads and thermal profiles — flat HVAC settings waste energy and compromise comfort.

Integration note: Evaluate Josh.ai as a unified control layer that integrates Ecobee HVAC + Lutron lighting + Soundtrack audio into a single scene-based trigger per daypart. This would allow one command to transition the full physical environment — lights, temperature, music — simultaneously rather than managing three separate systems.

Distinct from ConnectedFresh: ConnectedFresh monitors refrigeration/equipment energy (walk-ins, freezers). Ecobee monitors building HVAC energy (rooftop RTU, supplemental units, zone distribution).

name: Soundtrack
text_content:
What it is: Commercial business music platform — formerly Soundtrack Your Brand. Handles ASCAP, BMI, and SESAC performing rights licensing in one monthly subscription. The legal foundation for playing any music in a commercial environment.

Core capabilities:

Import existing Spotify playlists directly into a commercially licensed environment — no rebuild required
Daypart scheduling: different music programs per time window with automated transitions
Multi-zone audio control: independent programming per zone (interior vs. patio)
Volume scheduling
Central dashboard management
All three major US PROs covered in one subscription

Functions in stack:

Music Licensing & PRO Compliance
Daypart Music Scheduling
Music Zone Control
Outdoor Audio Zone Control

Why Soundtrack over alternatives: Music selection and programming is Brandon's creative domain — curated, not algorithmic. Soundtrack's Spotify import allows existing curation to deploy directly into a legal commercial environment. Rockbot is optimized for QSR algorithm-driven music; SoundMachine for multi-location enterprise control. Soundtrack is the right tool for a fine dining operator who has already built the musical identity and needs compliance infrastructure around it.

Pricing: ~$39–49/month. All PRO licenses included.

Legal note: Playing any music commercially without PRO licensing exposes the business to statutory damages of $750–$30,000 per song per incident. PRO inspectors (ASCAP, BMI, SESAC) actively visit restaurants.

name: TripleSeat
text_content:
What it is: Event management and sales platform for restaurants, hotels, and venues. Handles the full event lifecycle — inquiry through signed contract, BEO generation, deposit collection, and event execution.

Core capabilities:

Lead and inquiry management — captures all incoming event requests
Signable digital contracts with custom terms, deposits, and payment schedules
BEO (Banquet Event Order) generation — detailed event production documents for kitchen and service teams
Event proposals and menus
Deposit and payment processing
Client communication and CRM for event contacts
Reporting — event revenue pipeline, conversion rates, booked vs. forecasted

Functions in stack:

Event Contract Management
BEO Generation

Migration plan: TripleSeat is the current solution. Migrate to SevenRooms when they launch their native events/contracts product. SevenRooms already handles the inquiry and booking side; TripleSeat fills the BEO and contract gap that SevenRooms explicitly states is outside their current scope.

Integration: SevenRooms (inquiry → TripleSeat handoff for contract and BEO); Toast (event orders flow through POS); ClickUp (events pipeline reporting).

Pricing: Custom quoted — typically $100–300+/month depending on volume. Confirm current rate before contracting.

name: QuickBooks
text_content:
What it is: Small business accounting software. Industry standard for restaurant accounting — every CPA and external bookkeeper is fluent in it. Native integration with Restaurant365, which handles the operations layer and pushes data up to QuickBooks for the financial close.

Core capabilities:

General ledger and chart of accounts
Bank reconciliation — connects directly to bank accounts
Accounts payable and receivable
Financial reporting — P&L, balance sheet, cash flow statement
Budgeting and forecasting
Tax preparation support
Multi-user access (accountant + internal team)

Functions in stack:

Month-End Financial Close
Cash Flow Forecasting
General Ledger Management
Bookkeeping

Replaces: Rillet — which was an AI-native SaaS ERP built for subscription software companies, not restaurants. Wrong tool for a single-entity restaurant.

Why QuickBooks over Rillet: R365 has a native QuickBooks integration built and maintained. QuickBooks handles the financial close and reporting layer above R365. Rillet's strengths (multi-entity consolidation, subscription revenue recognition, SaaS-specific reporting) add zero value for a single restaurant entity. Rillet becomes relevant only if FNHG becomes a multi-entity holding company.

Integration: R365 Inventory & Purchasing → QuickBooks (native). Toast → QuickBooks (via R365). Rippling payroll → QuickBooks (native).

name: Canny
text_content:
What it is: Structured feedback and voting platform — repurposed as an internal employee feedback system. Same mechanics as a public product roadmap tool (idea submission, structured voting, status updates, categorized boards) but employees are the users, not customers. No public-facing component.

How it's used at FNHG:

Employees submit operational feedback, process improvement ideas, and concerns
Structured voting — employees upvote ideas that resonate
Categorized boards by department or topic (FOH, BOH, HR, Operations, Leadership)
Anonymous submission option for sensitive feedback
Status updates on ideas — employees see whether submissions are Under Review, Planned, or Declined
Closes the feedback loop — the critical difference from a suggestion box

Functions in stack:

Employee Feedback & Suggestions

Why Canny over a survey tool: Surveys are episodic. Canny is continuous and organized. Recurring friction points accumulate votes and become visible patterns — leadership can identify the top three operational problems at any given moment without running a survey.

Strategic alignment: Designed autonomy requires a real channel for employees to surface problems without social risk. Canny provides structure, visibility, and loop closure — feedback without follow-through breeds cynicism.

name: Every Angle
text_content:
What it is: Camera vision analytics software — hardware agnostic. Runs as a software layer on existing camera infrastructure including Rhombus hardware. Captures and analyzes in-venue visual data to produce marketing and operations intelligence.

Core capabilities:

Footfall counting and demographic analysis via camera vision
Heat mapping — shows where customers spend time in the space
Dwell time analytics — how long customers stay in specific zones
People counting — accurate in-venue occupancy tracking
Guest feedback surveys — post-visit feedback capture
Review response and reputation management — monitors and responds to reviews across platforms

Functions in stack:

Vision AI Analytics (Footfall & Demographics)
Heat Mapping
Dwell Time Analytics
People Counting
Guest Feedback Surveys
Review Response & Reputation Management

Relationship to Rhombus: Rhombus is the camera hardware and security layer. Every Angle is the analytics software layer running on top of the same Rhombus cameras. Both run simultaneously — Rhombus owns security, Every Angle owns guest analytics. Hardware agnostic means Every Angle is not tied to Rhombus; Rhombus is simply the camera infrastructure already installed.

NOT in scope: WiFi-based analytics (that is Bloom Intelligence's function).

name: Bloom Intelligence
text_content:
What it is: WiFi/MAC-based presence analytics, marketing automation, and AI reputation management platform. Captures customer presence data through WiFi network sensing — NOT camera or vision based.

Core capabilities:

Walk-by to walk-in conversion tracking — measures how many people who passed the venue actually entered, using WiFi/MAC device detection
Marketing attribution — ties WiFi visit data to campaign performance
Return visit tracking and visit frequency analytics via device recognition
AI reputation management — auto-responds to reviews in brand voice within minutes; sentiment analysis and at-risk guest recovery
CDP functions: customer profiles built from WiFi behavior data

Functions in stack:

Walk-By to Walk-In Conversion (WiFi-based — captures outside-the-venue foot traffic)
Marketing Attribution (WiFi-based — ties campaigns to in-store visits)

NOT in scope: Vision-based footfall, heat mapping, dwell time, people counting, or demographics. Those are camera vision functions that belong to Every Angle. Bloom captures WiFi signal presence; Every Angle captures what cameras see inside the venue. Different data sources, different functions, complementary outputs.

Relationship to Every Angle: Bloom covers the exterior (who walked by, who entered) via WiFi. Every Angle covers the interior (where they went, how long they stayed) via cameras.

name: PrepWizard
text_content:
What it is: Food prep labeling system. Prints use-by and expiration date labels on prepped food items via Bluetooth wireless label printer (Bixolon or Zebra). No ink or ribbon required. App on phone or tablet.

Core capabilities:

Automatic expiration date calculation based on product selected and current date/time — eliminates human error
Bulk label printing with one click for high-volume prep sessions
Custom label creation for catering orders and special batches
Cloud-based product catalog with shelf-life data preloaded per brand
Unlimited users per location — any employee can download the app and print

Functions in stack:

Food Prep Labeling & Expiration Date Printing (HACCP compliance requirement — all prepped food must carry a use-by label)

NOT in scope: Recipe costing, production planning (both belong to R365 Inventory & Purchasing).

Why it stays: R365 does not offer food labeling. This is a dedicated hardware + software system for a specific compliance workflow. Standalone, low-cost, high-impact function.

name: ConnectedFresh
text_content:
What it is: IoT environmental monitoring platform for food service operations. Wireless sensors (temperature, humidity, door open/close, energy, leak, air quality, occupancy) connected via LoRaWAN to a cellular gateway. Never touches the venue network. Hardware agnostic — bring your own sensors or use theirs.

Core capabilities:

Real-time sensor dashboard across all zones (walk-ins, freezers, prep areas, storage)
Custom threshold alerts via SMS, email, Slack, or voice call — fires in minutes, not hours
Automated HACCP-compliant temperature logs — no clipboards, no manual entry
Trend analytics and anomaly detection (early compressor failure detection)
Native integration with FoodDocs — sensor data auto-populates compliance documentation
Native integration with Restaurant365
API and webhooks for custom workflows (trigger ResQ work order on equipment anomaly)

Functions in stack:

Temperature & Cold Storage Monitoring (source layer — FoodDocs is the compliance layer above it)
Equipment Runtime / Health Monitoring (energy and telemetry data flags equipment issues before failure)

NOT in scope: Inventory management, purchasing, receiving, recipe costing. Those belong to R365 Inventory & Purchasing.

Setup: 15 minutes. Sensors arrive pre-configured. Cellular gateway, no IT project required.

text_content:

FNHG uses Inventory & Purchasing exclusively. Accounting belongs to QuickBooks. HR/payroll/scheduling belongs to Rippling.

Inventory Management — real-time inventory tracking across all items
Purchasing & Receiving — purchase orders, vendor management, delivery verification
Recipes — recipe costing, theoretical food cost calculation

Recipe Costing
Production Planning
Theoretical vs. Actual Food Cost
Sales Reporting & Analytics

Vendor & Supplier Management
